title: Imaging Cell Viability on Non-transparent Scaffolds — Using the Example of a Novel Knitted Titanium Implant
protocol: Clean the working area in the biosafety cabinet with 70% ethanol.
Prepare cell culture medium by mixing required components through sterile filters with a pore size of 0.22 µm.
Incubate 1 ml of prepared medium without cells at 37 °C, 5% CO2, 20% O2 and 90% humidity for 24 hours.
Check the sterility of the medium microscopically using a magnification of at least 200X after 24 hours.
Maintain SCP-1 cells in a standard cell culture incubator with conditions of 37 °C, 5% CO2, 20% O2 and 90% humidity.
Grow SCP-1 cells until they reach 80-90% confluency for maintenance or expansion.
Change the medium every 2-3 days during cell growth period.
Split SCP-1 cells at a ratio of 1:2 when reaching 80-90% confluency.
Warm culture medium and thaw trypsin/EDTA using a water bath at 37 °C for splitting cells.
Completely aspirate the culture medium from the 80-90% confluent cells and discard it into a waste container.
Wash the cells twice with DPBS.
Pipette 5 ml of DPBS onto T75 culture flask cells or 12 ml on T175 culture flask cells.
Aspirate and discard DPBS carefully.
Pipette 1 ml of 0.25% trypsin/EDTA onto T75 culture flask cells or 2 ml on T175 culture flask cells.
Incubate for 5-10 min at 37 °C in a standard cell culture incubator with 5% CO2, 20% O2 and 90% humidity.
Dislodge the cells by tapping the vessel and ensure all cells are detached from the culture plastic under the microscope.
Inactivate the trypsin reaction by adding 10 ml of culture medium to the cells.
Mix the trypsin and cells with the medium carefully by repeated pipetting.
Transfer the cell suspension into a reaction tube and centrifuge at 600 x g for 10 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 ml culture medium.
Count the cells using Trypan Blue exclusion method with a hemocytometer.
Clean the hemocytometer using tap water.
Dry the hemocytometer components using a lint-free tissue.
Moisten the cover glass and press it inversely onto the two glass runners on each side of the counting area.
Mix 10 µl of resuspended cells with 10 µl of 0.1% Trypan Blue solution to obtain a dilution factor of 2.
Load 10 µl of the total sample on the pre-cleaned and assembled hemocytometer chamber.
Count the number of live (white/transparent) cells on the 4x4 squares.
Count the number of dead (blue nuclei) cells on the 4x4 squares.
Calculate the total number of cells using the given formula.
Infect SCP-1 cells with replication-incompetent adenovirus particles coding for GFP.
Resuspend SCP-1 cells with a density of 50,000 cells/ml in culture medium.
Pipette 2 ml per well into a 6-well tissue culture plate.
Incubate at 37 °C in the standard cell culture incubator; 5% CO2, 20% O2 and 90% humidity.
At a confluency of 70-80%, without aspirating the culture medium, add 100 µl of adenovirus seed stock per 1 ml of culture medium.
Incubate for an hour in the standard cell culture incubator at 37 °C (5% CO2, 20% O2 and 90% humidity).
Remove the culture medium containing the virus seed stock and collect it for disposal.
Add fresh culture medium 2 ml per well of a 6-well-culture-plate to replenish.
Autoclave the virus particle-containing medium prior to disposal.
Place up to 5 scaffolds into a 50 ml reaction tube.
Wash the scaffold (6-7 mm thickness) three times with 30 ml distilled-deionized water for 20 min at room temperature, using rotor conditions (8 x g).
Replace the distilled-deionized water with 30 ml 1% (w/v) Triton-X-100 solution (dissolved in distilled-deionized water).
Wash the scaffolds once for 20 min at room temperature, using rotor conditions (8 x g).
Discard the Triton-X-100 solution.
Wash with 30 ml distilled-deionized water twice for 5 min each at room temperature.
Replace the distilled-deionized water.
Rinse scaffolds sequentially with reagent grade 99% acetone, 99% isopropanol, and 99% ethanol (30 ml each) for 2 x 5 min in an ultrasonic bath.
Wash scaffolds three times with 30 ml distilled-deionized water for 5 min.
Place scaffolds on a lint-free tissue to air dry overnight at room temperature.
Autoclave the scaffold for 15 min at 121 °C with 15 psi.
Prepare sulforhodamine B staining solution (0.04%) in 1% acetic acid and store at room temperature protected from light.
Immerse cleaned scaffold in 500 μl of sulforhodamine B staining solution using forceps.
Capture negative images of the scaffold using a fluorescence microscope.
Take pictures with an RFP LED cube/filter set at an excitation wavelength of 531/40 nm and an emission wavelength of 593/40 nm.
Alternatively, choose appropriate excitation and emission wavelengths based on the peak absorption and emission spectra of sulforhodamine B (excitation: 578 nm, emission: 593 nm).
Take pictures at lower magnifications (e.g., 4X or 10X) to visualize scaffold structure.
Determine characteristics such as pore size and shape using ImageJ software.
Take pictures at higher magnifications (e.g., 20X or 40X) to detect scaffold impurities, ensuring no dirt particles are present.
Pre-warm the culture medium at 37 °C in a water bath.
Place cleaned and sterilized scaffolds into each well of a 24-well tissue culture plate using forceps under a pre-cleaned biosafety cabinet.
Soak/incubate the scaffolds with 500 μl of culture medium for approximately 15 minutes to remove air from inside the scaffold.
Resuspend 500,000 Ad-GFP-infected SCP1 cells in 1 ml of culture medium.
Aspirate the medium completely off the scaffold after 15 minutes.
Dispense 100 µl of cell suspension on the scaffold placed in a 24-well plate.
Incubate for 30 min at 37 °C in a standard cell culture incubator (5% CO2, 20% O2 and 90% humidity).
Add 500 µl of culture medium.
Incubate for 24 hr in the standard cell culture incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2, 20% O2 and 90% humidity).
Evaluate cell adherence pattern and spreading on the scaffold surface using a fluorescence microscope.
Take pictures with a GFP LED cube/filter set at an excitation wavelength of 488 nm and an emission wavelength of 507 nm.
Capture pictures at lower magnifications (e.g., 4X or 10X) to visualize cell adherence patterns.
Observe cell spreading using a higher magnification (at least 100X).
Fix the cells with 4% formalin for further evaluation of cell spreading on the scaffold surface.
Proceed with conventional fluorescence staining of cellular structures, such as actin filaments, using phalloidin.
Adapt incubation times and fluorescent labelling of antibodies to fit individual scaffold characteristics, including diffusion times or auto-fluorescence.
Change the culture medium the next day to remove non-adherent cells.
Calculate the percentage of adherent cells on the scaffold by resazurin conversion measurement.
Completely aspirate the culture medium from SCP-1 cells and discard it into a waste container.
Wash SCP-1 cells once with DPBS to remove detached cells.
Add 500 μl DPBS per well of the 24-well tissue culture plate containing SCP-1 cells on the scaffold.
Cover the cells with a required amount of sterile resazurin working solution (0.25% resazurin in culture medium).
Incubate at 37 °C in the standard cell culture incubator (5% CO2, 20% O2 and 90% humidity) for 30 min.
Include at least one well with the resazurin working solution but without cells as a background control, and incubate under the same conditions.
Transfer 100 μl conditioned supernatant from each well of the 24-well tissue culture plate into a 96-microwell plate.
Wash remaining cells three times with 1 ml DPBS for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove residual resazurin working solution after the third wash.
Add culture medium to implants with SCP-1 cells (500 μl per well of the 24-well tissue culture plate).
Incubate plates at 37 °C in a standard cell culture incubator (5% CO2, 20% O2 and 90% humidity) for further time course measurements.
Set up replicates to minimize pipetting errors.
Place the 96-microwell plate into the microplate reader.
Measure fluorescence of formed resorufin at an excitation wavelength of 545 nm and emission wavelength of 585 nm.
Alternatively, choose adequate excitation and emission wavelengths with a fluorescence spectral viewer.
Measure the fluorescence of formed resorufin in conditioned medium using a bottom optic.
Adjust the gain on the microplate reader by pipetting a resorufin standard curve, ensuring the fluorescent signal is below 80% of the maximum detectable signal (20,000).
Subtract the background signal from the test samples.
Calculate the percentage of viability of the cells on the scaffold using a standard curve for each cell line used.
Analyze cell growth/proliferation by estimating the relative increase in resazurin conversion throughout the cultivation time, setting day 1 as reference.
Freshly prepare the resazurin working solution for analysis.
Ensure incubation times are equal between different measurements.
Repeat the entire protocol of resazufin conversion measurement at least three times to get consistent results.
Plate SCP1 cells on the scaffold with a seeding density of 50,000 cells/scaffold and allow it to grow under standard cell culture conditions.
Aspirate and discard the culture medium from SCP-1 cells after 24-48 hours.
Wash SCP-1 cells once with DPBS to remove detached cells.
Add 500 μl DPBS per well of the 24-well tissue culture plate.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Stain SCP-1 cells using fluorophores: calcein AM, Hoechst 33342, and ethidium homodimer simultaneously.
Set an incubation time to 30 minutes in the dark.
Optimize incubation times based on scaffold characteristics (pore size, depth).
Incubate with calcein AM at a final concentration of 2 μM for viable cell detection.
Incubate with Hoechst 33342 at a final concentration of 0.002 µg/µl for total cell detection.
Incubate with ethidium homodimer at a final concentration of 4 μM for dead cell detection.
Wash cells three times with DPBS (1 ml per well) for each 5 minutes at room temperature.
Take pictures using a fluorescence microscope immediately after washing.
Take pictures of the calcein (living cells) with a GFP LED cube/filter set (excitation wavelength of 470/22 nm, emission wavelength of 510/42 nm).
Alternatively choose an adequate excitation and emission wavelength with the help of the fluorescence spectral viewer.
Take pictures of the Hoechst 33342 with a DAPI LED cube/filter set (excitation wavelength of 357/44 nm, emission wavelength of 447/60 nm).
Alternatively choose the adequate excitation and emission wavelength with the help of the fluorescence spectral viewer.
Take pictures of the ethidium homodimer with a RFP LED cube/filter set (excitation wavelength of 531/40 nm, emission wavelength of 593/40 nm).
Alternatively choose the adequate excitation and emission wavelength with the help of the fluorescence spectral viewer.
